title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Measures for Hearing Defense Lawyers' Opinions in Death Penalty Review Cases
keywords_en: concerning the handling of death penalty review cases
full_text_en:
Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Measures for Hearing the Opinions of Defense Lawyers in Death Penalty Review Cases

Fa [2014] No. 346

To: The High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; all local intermediate people's courts throughout the country; all military courts of major military units; and all intermediate people's courts of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

The Supreme People's Court's Measures for Hearing the Opinions of Defense Lawyers in Death Penalty Review Cases are hereby issued for your compliance and implementation.

December 29, 2014

Measures for Hearing the Opinions of Defense Lawyers in Death Penalty Review Cases

These Measures are formulated in accordance with the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Lawyers Law of the People's Republic of China, and relevant legal provisions, for the purpose of effectively ensuring that defense lawyers for defendants in death penalty review cases exercise the right to defense according to law and ensuring the quality of death penalty review cases.

Article 1 A defense lawyer in a death penalty review case may inquire with the Case Filing Division of the Supreme People's Court about case filing information. When making such an inquiry, the defense lawyer shall provide his or her own name, the name of the law firm, the name of the defendant, the cause of action, as well as the name of the High People's Court that submitted the case for review and the case number.

If the Case Filing Division of the Supreme People's Court can give an immediate reply, it shall do so; if it cannot give an immediate reply, it shall reply within two working days. The content of the reply shall include whether the case has been filed and the adjudication division handling the case.

Article 2 When a lawyer accepts the appointment of the defendant or the close relatives of the defendant, or the assignment of a legal aid institution, to serve as a defense lawyer in a death penalty review case, the lawyer shall, within three working days from the date of accepting the appointment or assignment, submit the relevant formalities to the relevant adjudication division of the Supreme People's Court.

The defense lawyer shall submit the defense opinion within one and a half months from the date of accepting the appointment or assignment.

Article 3 When a defense lawyer submits written materials such as appointment formalities, legal aid formalities, defense opinions, and evidence, such materials may, with the consent of the High People's Court, be collected on its behalf and transferred with the case file, or may be sent by mail to the adjudication division handling the case of the Supreme People's Court, or be submitted when presenting opinions in person. For cases not yet filed, the defense lawyer may send such materials by mail to the Case Filing Division of the Supreme People's Court, and the Case Filing Division shall, after filing the case, transfer them with the case file.

Article 4 A defense lawyer may go to the office premises of the Supreme People's Court to review, excerpt, and copy case file materials. However, materials that shall not be disclosed according to law shall not be reviewed, excerpted, or copied.

Article 5 Where a defense lawyer requests to present opinions in person, the judge handling the case shall arrange it in a timely manner.

Generally, the judge handling the case and the court clerk shall hear the opinions of the defense lawyer in person. Alternatively, other members of the collegial panel or all members thereof, together with the court clerk, may hear the opinions in person.

Article 6 Hearing the opinions of a defense lawyer in person shall be conducted at the office premises of the Supreme People's Court or a local people's court. The defense lawyer may bring a paralegal to attend. The persons hearing the opinions in person shall verify the identities of the defense lawyer and the paralegal.

Article 7 When hearing the opinions of a defense lawyer in person, a record shall be made and signed by the defense lawyer, and then attached to the case file. Where the defense lawyer submits relevant materials, such materials shall be accepted and a receipt list in duplicate shall be prepared, with one copy handed to the defense lawyer and the other copy attached to the case file.

Article 8 When hearing the opinions of a defense lawyer in person, the people's court, if conditions permit, shall assign personnel to record the entire process by audio and video. Other persons present shall not make their own audio or video recordings or take photographs.

Article 9 After the conclusion of the review, the people's court entrusted to pronounce the judgment shall, within five working days after the pronouncement, serve the judgment document of the Supreme People's Court to the defense lawyer.

Article 10 These Measures shall take effect as of February 1, 2015.
